course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Equations and Inequalities
unit.blurb: Constructing and solving linear equations (including brackets and fractions), simultaneous equations, and inequalities on a number line.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Construct and solve linear equations with unknowns on both sides, brackets and fractions.

O2.t: Solve a pair of simultaneous linear equations by substitution or elimination, and link the solution to where two lines meet.

O3.t: Construct and solve linear inequalities, show solutions on a number line and list integer solutions.

p: An equation stays true if you do **the same thing to both sides**. Collect the unknown on one side and the numbers on the other.
With brackets, **expand first**. With fractions, **multiply every term** by the denominator (or the lowest common multiple of the denominators).

p: **Simultaneous equations** are two equations that are true at the same time. The solution is the pair (x, y) that fits both – it is where the two **lines cross**.
**Substitution:** if one equation says y = …, put that expression into the other equation. **Elimination:** add or subtract the equations so that one unknown disappears.
Draw both lines on the same grid. The coordinates of the crossing point are the solution.
Always check your answer in BOTH original equations – if it only fits one, something went wrong.

p: < less than, ≤ less than or equal to, > greater than, ≥ greater than or equal to.
On a number line, an **open circle** ○ means the end value is **not included** (< or >). A **filled circle** ● means it **is included** (≤ or ≥).
If you multiply or divide both sides by a **negative** number, **reverse the inequality sign**: −2x < 8 → x > −4.
x > 2 does NOT include 2: draw an open circle at 2.
